title: Microsoft Places: availability in the GCC cloud
notes: claim 80: severity blocker on a rationale: risk rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the page reports the GCC arrival default as on while acknowledging that Microsoft has not confirmed that default. Its licensing guidance also omits the Teams Premium transition exception and restrictions on free Single Space entitlements, and its statement that Learn documents no GCC differences overlooks documented GCC autorelease support.

claims.claim: No admin UI for the SpaceAnalyticsEnabled feature setting is documented.

claims.claim: EnableBuildings has an effect only after buildings and floors are configured.

claims.claim: Places finder OID scoping requires a mail-enabled security group rather than a standard security group.
claims.quote: If you plan to use a standard security group, your configuration may not work as expected. To ensure proper functionality, the security group must be set as a mail-enabled security group.

claims.claim: Feature-access scoping allows at most 20 OIDs.

claims.claim: OID-based scoping is supported only for PlacesFinderEnabled, and the other settings are tenant-wide.

The Enable Places analytics page nevertheless gives a SpaceAnalyticsEnabled OID-scoping example, and the turn-off page describes group scoping for core settings; these pages disagree.' Keep the existing citations to all three pages.

claims.claim: The four tenant feature settings use Set-PlacesSettings in the MicrosoftPlaces module, running PowerShell 7 after Connect-MicrosoftPlaces.
claims.quote: Make sure to launch PowerShell7 as an Administrator, and connect to the Microsoft Places node using Connect-MicrosoftPlaces. ... Install-Module -Name MicrosoftPlaces -Force

claims.claim: Microsoft's organisation-wide turn-off procedure disables EnablePlacesWebApp and EnableBuildings and then disables Places Enhanced for all users.
claims.quote: Turn off Places Core features using tenant settings, then disable the Places Enhanced service plan for all users ... Set-PlacesSettings -EnablePlacesWebApp 'Default:false' ... Set-PlacesSettings -EnableBuildings 'Default:false'

claims.claim: The Places Management web app manages directory objects and their reservation settings.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Places Management web application enables Places, Building, and Desk Admins to manage the Places directory, including creating and deleting desks and rooms, configuring desk modes and reservation settings, and identifying unassigned desks.

claims.claim: The documented Management web app does not expose the four tenant feature settings.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Places admin portal feature settings EnablePlacesWebApp EnableBuildings PlacesFinderEnabled SpaceAnalyticsEnabled user interface. Opened admin-web-app and read Administration Portal search excerpt; documented UI manages directory objects and views analytics, not feature switches.

claims.claim: EnablePlacesWebApp must be on for administrators to access the Management web app.
claims.quote: The "EnablePlacesWebApp" setting must be enabled for the tenant in order for the admin users to access the Management Web App.

claims.claim: Places Administrator can enable and disable Places features.
claims.quote: Places Administrator ... Enable and disable Microsoft Places features

claims.claim: Get-PlacesSettings shows the tenant's configured Places feature settings.
claims.quote: You can use Get-PlacesSettings to view all Microsoft Places features settings configured on your tenant.

claims.claim: Tenant settings in the MicrosoftPlaces PowerShell module cover each Places feature.
claims.quote: rationale: 'tenant settings in the MicrosoftPlaces PowerShell module cover each feature'; Governance controls: 'Whether users can make their work location visible to others is a separate mailbox calendar configuration setting in Exchange Online.'
claims.fix: Replace the rationale's final clause with: 'the documented tenant settings control app access, building visibility, Places finder and analytics.'

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout, hierarchy setup
claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to configure the building and floor hierarchy, but that control has no table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Build the building and floor hierarchy from room lists with Initialize-Places'; controls table covers app access, building visibility, finder access, analytics access and Places Enhanced, not hierarchy creation.
claims.fix: The hierarchy-configuration checklist step has no corresponding controls-table row; remove that checklist bullet. Keep the existing prerequisite explanation in Scope.
